text:
Maria Chen: quick RFC follow-up — we need to decide the shape of the SDK client surface for pagination+retries across py/ts/go. do we keep retry/pagination behavior in the transport, or push it to the language SDK layer?

Devin Patel: my take: transport should provide primitives (send, stream, meta) and the SDK languages compose ergonomic helpers (iterators, generators). keep transport small. :thumbsup:

Hao Li: +1 on primitives but + concern: error semantics differ across languages (exceptions vs error values). we should define a common RetryPolicy model (idempotency, max_attempts, backoff) that transports implement and SDKs map to local idioms.

Samir Kapoor: also consider batching/backpressure. if retries are transport-level and invisible, they can interact badly with continuous batching. proposal: transport exposes retry hooks and a retryable flag on requests so batching layer can decide to re-enqueue vs drop.

Maria Chen: what about pagination tokens? do we return raw tokens to users or wrap as iterators? streaming endpoints complicate this.

Devin Patel: examples:

Python (proposal):
```
# iterator hides tokens
for page in client.responses.list(inputs):
    for item in page.items:
        process(item)
```
TypeScript: async iterator -> `for await (const item of client.responses.listAll())`
Go: return a `ListPager` with `Next() (Item, error)` or channel-backed iterator depending on style.

Hao Li: those are good. to unify, add a small metadata envelope from transport: `meta: { next_token, estimated_cost, retryable }`. transports must not attempt high-level pagination decisions (like automatic dedup across pages). SDKs implement the paging loop.

Samir Kapoor: I'd prefer default retries enabled but visible: returned error types should include `Retryable: bool` and `RetryAfter: seconds` so SDKs can either auto-retry or surface to users. Avoid opaque retrying inside the transport unless it's only idempotent-safe fast-ish retries (eg 3 attempts with jitter).

Maria Chen: streaming + function-calls: streaming should be a separate surface (stream iterator) and not mixed with paged iterator. function-calls and tool-calling might require partial-result retries — tricky. we should document recommended patterns and provide a `StreamingAdapter` in each SDK that implements reconnect semantics plus an opt-out.

Devin Patel: quick sketch of the RetryPolicy model to standardize across SDKs:
```
RetryPolicy = {
  mode: "none" | "standard" | "aggressive",
  maxAttempts: int,
  baseBackoffMs: int,
  maxBackoffMs: int,
  idempotency: "unsafe" | "idempotent"
}
```
transport attaches `x-retryable` header to responses for non-2xx transient cases.

Hao Li: can we also add a `RetryContext` that SDKs populate (user metadata, route, estimated token cost) so transport can compute cost-aware decisions? but that couples them. maybe optional.

Samir Kapoor: action: split into two PRs — 1) transport/headers + RetryPolicy schema, 2) SDK ergonomic wrappers (iterators/streams). keep the RFC minimal for landing. also add perf tests for batching+retry interplay.

deploy-bot: new PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/421 (RFC: SDK client adapter shape + retry/paging guide)

Maria Chen: awesome. I'll update the RFC per samir's split and add test checklist. can someone volunteer to write the TypeScript iterator impl? @Devin? :coffee:

Devin Patel: I can prototype the TS async iterator this week. will add examples for `list()` vs `listAll()` and a `withRetry(policy)` wrapper.

Hao Li: I'll draft the RetryPolicy protobuf/IDL and make sure Go/Py mappers are straightforward.

Samir Kapoor: I'll own the perf tests and a short doc on batching interactions.

Maria Chen: perfect — I'll update the RFC and move to final review. thanks all.

(Reaction thread: :thumbsup: from Devin, :eyes: from Hao)
